prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer
There isn’t a single “best” one‑click service that tells you whether ChatGPT (and other LLMs) will recommend your business. The practical approach is a two‑part strategy: (A) make sure your business is present in the data sources LLMs use (Google Business Profile, Bing, Apple, major directories, structured data), and (B) actively test and monitor LLM outputs with a mix of direct queries and local‑SEO / monitoring tools.  

What I recommend (highest ROI)
1. Claim and optimize Google Business Profile (GBP), Bing Places, Apple Business Register and major directories (Yelp, TripAdvisor, etc.). Many LLMs and chat assistants draw on those sources or on search results derived from them.
2. Use a knowledge‑graph/distribution tool such as Yext (or similar listing management services) to push consistent, up‑to‑date business data to many endpoints — this increases the chance AI models will see the correct info.
3. Monitor local visibility with local‑SEO tools: BrightLocal, Whitespark, Moz Local or SEMrush (Local/Listing Management). These show local pack rankings and citation consistency that materially affect whether assistants will surface you.
4. Test directly against LLMs (ChatGPT, Google Bard/Gemini, Bing Chat, Anthropic Claude):
   - Query multiple models with location and intent: e.g., “Recommend a plumber near 94110 that does emergency calls and has good reviews.”  
   - Try variations: “best”, “near me”, “open now”, “cheap”, category + location.  
   - Use browsing‑enabled versions or tools that use live web data when possible (ChatGPT with browsing or plugins; Bing Chat) because base models without browsing can be out of date or hallucinate.
5. Automate repeated checks if you want ongoing monitoring: write small scripts that call public LLM APIs or use testing tools (OpenAI API, Anthropic, Google) to run a battery of prompts and record outputs.

Why these steps
- LLMs often pull from knowledge graphs, search indexes and directories more than isolated websites. If your GBP/structured data is accurate and widely distributed, you’re much likelier to be recommended.
- Local SEO tools (BrightLocal, Whitespark, Moz/SEMrush) quantify how you appear in the local pack and directories — the same signals AIs use.
- Direct testing across multiple models shows whether a particular assistant will surface you and reveals wording that helps.

Concrete tools and what each does
- Google Business Profile + Bing Places + Apple Business Register: primary sources to control how you appear.
- Yext (or similar listing management): distributes authoritative business data to many partner platforms and makes it easier for AI/knowledge graphs to find consistent info.
- BrightLocal / Whitespark / Moz Local / SEMrush Local: track local rankings, citation consistency, review aggregation.
- Social/mentions monitoring: Google Alerts, Brand24, Mention — useful because web mentions feed the indexes LLMs may consult.
- Direct model testing: OpenAI ChatGPT (including GPT‑4/gpt‑4o if you have access), Bing Chat, Google Bard/Gemini, Anthropic Claude — test manually or via APIs.

Sample test prompts to use
- “Recommend 3 Italian restaurants within 2 miles of [ZIP/coordinate]. Explain why and give phone and hours.”
- “I’m in [city]; what is a highly rated small plumbing business that handles emergency calls?”
- “If someone in [neighborhood] asks for a florist that does same‑day delivery, what would you recommend and why?”

Pitfalls to watch for
- LLM hallucinations — they may invent businesses or wrong details. If an assistant recommends a competitor, verify sources cited (if any).
- No universal ranking — different models draw on different data and can behave differently by prompt and time.
- Some models aren’t “live” and use stale knowledge; always use browsing/live versions for current recommendations.

If you want, I can:
- Run a small set of test prompts against ChatGPT/Bing/Bard for your business (tell me business name, address/ZIP, and 3 example queries), or
- Recommend a concrete monitoring stack (which tools to buy and how to set up automated checks) based on your budget. Which would you prefer?
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
